com.addr.hunterj.jdbc
Interface JdbcQueryHandler

All Known Implementing Classes:
AbstractQueryHandler
public interface JdbcQueryHandler

Except for the ConnectionAdapter, the JdbcQueryHandler is the only interface that the user need implement to use this framework. Each query is encapsulated within doQueryAndProcessResults() completely. 

 Statement stmt = getConnection().createStatement();
 ResultSet results = stmt.executeQuery(sqlQuery);
 while(results.next(){
         ...
 }
No need for additional callbacks. No need to close any of the JDBC resources. All that is taken care of. The recommended approach is to extend AbstractQueryHandler.

Version:
1.0
Author:
Jim Hunter

isHaltOnError

boolean isHaltOnError()
Called by the framework to determine if execution of given set of JdbcQueryHandlers should be halted in the event of an exception thrown by doQueryAndProcessResults().

Returns:
the value of the haltOnError switch

setHaltOnError

void setHaltOnError(boolean haltOnError)
The haltOnError switch is initialized to true by default. It is used to determine if execution of a given set of JdbcQueryHandler instances will be halted in the event of an exception thrown by doQueryAndProcessResults(). Users can set this switch to true to prevent termination of all queries if this query throws an exception.

Parameters:
haltOnError -

executeNested

void executeNested(JdbcQueryHandler queryHandler)
                   throws java.sql.SQLException
Provides support for nested queries. Some queries require that an additional java.sql.Statement be created and invoked within the scope of the first query, i.e., before the outer Statement and ResultSet have been closed. Resources within inner-most nested JdbcQueryHandler instances will be closed before those within the containing JdbcQueryHandler.

Parameters:
queryHandler -
Throws:
java.sql.SQLException
